options: A named, stored connection definition to a remote data source, via an OLE DB provider
A new SQL Server login
A new Agent job
A firewall rule for remote connections
questions.explain: sp_addlinkedserver defines the linked server itself — its name and the OLE DB provider/data source it points to — but doesn't handle authentication.

questions.q: What does @useself = N'True' in sp_addlinkedsrvlogin do?
options: Passes through the connecting user's own credentials to authenticate on the remote server
Disables the linked server entirely
Forces the linked server to use SQL authentication only
Creates a new remote login automatically
questions.explain: useself=True passes through the caller's own security context, which works cleanly only with proper Windows delegation or matching SQL logins on both sides.

questions.q: Why is @useself = N'False' with an explicit mapped login generally preferred in production?
options: It doesn't depend on Kerberos delegation being configured correctly
It's the only option that supports SQL Server-to-SQL Server links
It automatically encrypts all remote traffic
It removes the need for sp_addlinkedserver entirely
questions.explain: Pass-through authentication (useself=True) requires working delegation; an explicit local-to-remote login mapping is more predictable and doesn't have that dependency.

questions.q: Can sp_addlinkedserver be used to connect to a non-SQL Server source like Oracle or an ODBC system?
options: Yes — by specifying a different OLE DB provider in the @provider parameter
No — sp_addlinkedserver only supports SQL Server to SQL Server links
Only if the remote source is converted to a SQL Server database first
Only through SQL Server Agent, never through sp_addlinkedserver
questions.explain: The same sp_addlinkedserver call links to non-SQL Server sources by naming a different installed OLE DB provider — Oracle, ODBC, flat files, etc.

questions.q: What is required on the local instance to link to a non-SQL Server OLE DB source?
options: The relevant OLE DB provider must actually be installed on the local machine
Nothing extra — all providers ship built into SQL Server by default
The remote source must be migrated to SQL Server first
SQL Server Agent must be running
questions.explain: Linking to a non-SQL Server source depends on that source's OLE DB (or ODBC-via-OLE DB) provider being installed and available on the local server.
